mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with negative returns (correlation coefficient < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which is often a precursor to an economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 declines do not correlate with negative returns (correlation coefficient < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO drops > 2% MoM do not correlate with negative returns (correlation coefficient < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between FEDFUNDS > 2% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with negative returns (interaction term p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS growth does not correlate with positive returns (correlation coefficient < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and retail sales (RSAFS) also decline, it signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY decline > 10% and RSAFS MoM decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between HOUST and RSAFS declines does not correlate with negative returns (interaction term p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of economic expansion, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% year-over-year signals increased economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO growth > 3% YoY does not correlate with positive returns (correlation coefficient < 0.1).
